subject: general
question: The Himalayan Mountain range was formed by the collision of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Plate and Eurasian Plate.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Himalayan Mountain range** was formed by the collision of the **Eurasian Plate and the Indian Plate.**
 
• This collision began around **50 million years ago** and is still ongoing, causing the Himalayas to rise at a rate of about **5 mm per year.**
 
• The collision of the two plates caused the Indian Plate to be pushed underneath the** Eurasian Plate,** creating immense pressure and heat that led to the formation of the** Himalayan Mountains. **
 
• The Himalayas are the **highest and youngest mountain range** in the world and are home to some of the **tallest peaks**, including Mount Everest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **African Plate** and** Australian Plate** are both located far away from the **Indian Plate and Eurasian Plate**, making it impossible for them to have contributed to the formation of the Himalayas.
 
• The collision between the** Indian Plate and African Plate **did occur, but it happened much earlier, around **200 million years ago**, and led to the formation of the **supercontinent Gondwana.**
 
• **The Eurasian Plate** is the largest tectonic plate on Earth, covering most of **Europe and Asia**.
 
 
• It is also responsible for the formation of other mountain ranges, such as the **Alps and the Ural Mountains.**
